newsitem.title: USA: IBM plans big move to cut PC ownership costs.
newsitem.headline: IBM plans big move to cut PC ownership costs.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. is expected to announce a major initiative Monday aimed at lowering the cost of owning, maintaining and upgrading personal computers for its corporate customers.

The computer giant plans to offer a one-stop shopping package so that customers can lease PC hardware for a monthly fee that will cover financing, service, maintenance, support, and upgrades, said sources close to IBM.
A spokesman for IBM's PC Co., the business unit behind the initiative, said IBM does not comment on unannounced products.

The package, which has been code-named Spruce, will be offered by IBM and its authorized resellers and partners as it seeks to meet increased competition from the direct sellers of PCs, Dell Computer Corp. and Gateway 2000 Inc., which have lower costs.

As part of the package, IBM will announce that it is consolidating its two PC hardware lines aimed at corporate users into one, the IBM PC 300. IBM will eliminate the IBM PC 700. The 300 will have a better look and be easier to upgrade, the sources said.
IBM's big move comes amid an increasing amount of concern in the computer industry on the cost of owning PCs.

Since companies such as Sun Microsystems Inc. and Oracle Corp. have been touting the advantages of the network computer, a scaled-down device used to access the Internet and corporate networks, they have also highlighted the high cost of PC ownership. Some recent market studies have estimated the cost from $6,000 to $12,000 a year, per PC.

"The whole intent is to reduce the cost of ownership, not just the cost of the PC," said one industry analyst, who asked not to be named. "The major issue today has to do with life cycle costs, not only the maintaining the PC but the support organization behind it, the security ... and obsolescence."

IBM will also work with its business partners in the 13 different industries that it focuses on, so that these partners can develop custom programs and software applications for specific areas, such as the insurance, banking, travel, the sources said.
The IBM PC Co. will also work closely with the IBM Credit Corp., its credit and financing subsidiary, which is making available $17 billion in financing for corporate resellers.
Resellers are companies that resell computers to corporate users, offering service, support and increasingly, the actual assembly of machines, in partnership with PC makers.

Analysts said that one of the many advantages of IBM's new plan is that a corporation could exchange the PCs, servers or laptops it leases from IBM and replace them with more current technology, which changes more rapidly each year.

"People with 10 or even five PCs don't want to be obsolete but they don't want to redo everything every six months," said another analyst, who asked not to be named. "They will outsource the worry and the manageability. The cost of ownership with be the least outlay."
They also will not have to worry about servicing, customer support and upgrading software or peripherals such as memory.
